notes: COM with a body-part nominal probe; meaning is deliberately left to context.
LOC converb; construction-first temporal overlap test.
COM converb with switch-reference; retained as a matched discourse contrast.
Agentive participial relative using CLOSE; the head noun is the understood agent of the participial predicate.
Patientive participial relative using CLOSE; the head noun is the understood patient.
LOC + neutral direction + APPL: the person is promoted as the core relational participant while the LOC relation remains statically anchored.
CONTAINMENT + neutral direction + APPL: the bounded place/domain itself is promoted as the core relational participant; the ordinary 3P-inanimate object index is zero.

translation: I move onto the tool / establish contact with the tool.
notes: POSITION + i- + APPL: the inanimate support/contact participant is promoted; i- supplies entry into or establishment of the configuration.

translation: I move off the tool / terminate contact with the tool.
notes: POSITION + a- + APPL: the inanimate support/contact participant is promoted; a- supplies departure from or termination of the configuration.

translation: I sit on the tool / remain in contact with the tool.
notes: POSITION + neutral direction + APPL: the support/contact configuration is treated as an existing relation and the support participant is promoted without directed change.
COM + neutral direction + APPL: the associated person is promoted as a core participant without an inherent benefit/harm interpretation.

translation: I move away from the person.
notes: LOC + a- + APPL: the landmark is promoted as a core source/reference from which the event diverges.

translation: I do not hold the tool.
notes: Active negation test: -su- follows agreement and precedes tense; the ordinary 3P-inanimate object remains unindexed.
Active polar-question test using verbal -y- in the discourse slot; the final form is kutye after repair of prohibited -yi.
Plural subject pronoun with person-only verbal agreement; no number distinction appears on the verb.
Active genitive NP test: the GEN-marked possessor precedes the head noun.
Finite relative clause follows the head noun and uses a gap for the relativized patient; no relative pronoun or resumptive is added.

translation: As for the tool, I hold it.
notes: Topic-left test: the topicalized object is moved to the left edge without changing its ABS role.
Matched focus test: the object is immediately preverbal and receives narrow prosodic prominence; the segmental form is unchanged from neutral SOV order.

text: Neku tak kuci, seku ren kuci.
translation: I hold the tool; you hold the person.
segmentation: ne-ku tak k-u-k-i se-ku ren k-u-t-i
notes: Coordination by juxtaposition: independent clauses are simply juxtaposed without an overt conjunction.
Experiencer-valency probe: the experiencer is ERG and the stimulus is ABS. This tests one lexical alignment without establishing a universal experiencer case.
Perception-valency probe: SMELL uses an ordinary ABS stimulus here; compare with FEAR and PERCEIVE before generalizing experiencer alignment.

translation: I tell the person that I am carrying.
notes: Speech-valency probe: bare nominalized content is combined with a recipient/goal LOC phrase. This tests a finite SAY clause with a nominalized complement and does not yet establish a universal speech-complement construction.
Search/hunt-valency probe: HUNT takes a direct ABS target in this test. A distinct SEARCH lexeme is not currently established.
ACQUIRE/OBTAIN-valency probe: the broadened `n` root takes an ordinary ABS object. FIND remains an available lexical interpretation rather than a separate grammatical frame.

translation: I build the tool with stone.
notes: Material/medium probe: COM expresses the stone relation as an event-oriented means/material participant. This does not promote a dedicated MATERIAL or SOURCE case, and GEN is not generalized to event arguments by this example.
Simple imperative: ka- marks IMP, ordinary person agreement is suppressed, and HOLD uses its citation/nonfinite form ka.
Transitive imperative: the ordinary 3P animate object index remains available even though subject agreement is suppressed.
Directional imperative: i- remains outside ka-, preserving the independent relational vector.
Directional imperative: a- remains outside ka-, preserving divergence independently of mood.
Prohibitive: NEG is composed with imperative; person agreement remains suppressed. Surface sequencing follows the verbal template after the imperative stem.
Hortative: the imperative construction is reused with an overt 1PL ERG subject; the verb still lacks ordinary person agreement.
Necessity modal auxiliary: finite morphology is carried by the auxiliary; the lexical predicate is citation/nonfinite.
Possibility modal auxiliary: finite morphology is carried by the auxiliary; the lexical predicate is citation/nonfinite.
Intention modal auxiliary: finite morphology is carried by the auxiliary; the lexical predicate is citation/nonfinite.

translation: Perhaps I am sleeping / I am apparently sleeping.
notes: Clause-level epistemic/evidential particle with broad scope over an ordinary finite clause.
Past necessity: tense remains on the finite modal auxiliary while the lexical predicate remains nonfinite.

translation: I must move toward the person.
notes: Modal auxiliary plus directed lexical complement: relational direction remains on the lexical predicate while finiteness remains on the modal auxiliary.

translation: I may move toward the person.
notes: Possibility + directed lexical complement: modality and relational direction remain independent.
